# AGENTS.md: settle-mcp, for the assistant reading this

You are connected to settle-mcp: an MCP server that explains SETTLE and KANERVA, sets them up on your machine, and runs them. Read this document first, then the guide for the person you are helping, then call tools.

## Who you are helping

Three kinds of reader come here, and each has a guide written in their own terms: what this is, how to use it in a project (SETTLE alone, the KANERVA memory alone, the two together), one real example with its real output, a getting-started, and links into the detailed docs. Find out which reader you have and read that guide before anything else; `read_doc` takes the name, and each is a resource.

- a programmer or computer scientist: `read_doc {"name": "who-you-are/for-programmers"}` or the resource `site://who-you-are/for-programmers`. You write a model as a short text of yes-or-no things, how much each one leans, and how much pairs of them pull on each other. A machine then flips the coins and settles. You ask it questions and it answers with counts. That is SETTLE. KANERVA is a memory that stores long bit patterns and finds one again from a damaged copy. settle-mcp is a server that hands both to an assistant over the Model Context Protocol.
- a visual artist: `read_doc {"name": "who-you-are/for-visual-artists"}` or the resource `site://who-you-are/for-visual-artists`. A picture here is a field of lights. Each light is a coin that keeps being tossed, with a bias toward the picture it wants to be and a pull toward its neighbours. Out of noise the picture forms, holds, breaks up again when the field is heated, and forms again. SETTLE is the language that describes such a field. KANERVA is a memory that stores pictures as bit patterns and brings one back from a smudged copy. settle-mcp hands both to an assistant, so you can ask for a program instead of writing one.
- a sound artist: `read_doc {"name": "who-you-are/for-sound-artists"}` or the resource `site://who-you-are/for-sound-artists`. Every picture on this site is a field of coins settling, and every one of them can be heard. settle-hear makes sound from a settle's own numbers: the temperature becomes hiss, the flips become crackle, the energy becomes a falling drone, the match with the stored picture becomes a chord that resolves. SETTLE is the language that describes the field; KANERVA is a memory that stores bit patterns, a rhythm or a chord voicing among them, and finds one from a damaged copy; settle-mcp hands both to an assistant.

The folder index is `site://who-you-are`. When the reader is none of the three, start with the programmer guide and say so.

## What this is

- SETTLE is a small language for settling machines: name yes-or-no things, give them leans and pulls, hold what you know, let the machine settle, and ask it questions. The interpreter is settle-rs, a Rust binary.
- KANERVA is the Rust crate for sparse distributed memory SETTLE uses: write long bit patterns, read one back from a noisy read-address, refuse one that was never stored.
- settle-mcp is this server. The website is the source of truth. These docs are generated from the SETTLE site (its pages, its English strings, the SETTLE docs and the KANERVA README it shows) by `tools/build_mcp_docs.mjs`. Never edit a generated file by hand; change the site and rebuild.

## Where each reader starts

- A programmer: `help` with a topic, `list_examples`, `get_example`, then `check_system` and `setup` (a dry run until confirmed), then `run_program` and `sdm_store_recall`.
- A visual artist: the guide first; then `sdm_store_recall` with their own patterns, and `run_program` on the picture program in the guide. The drawing library, settle-see, is a folder of plain JavaScript named in the guide.
- A sound artist: the guide first; then `run_program` on a model that chooses a chord voicing by annealing. The hearing library, settle-hear, and its voices table are named in the guide.

## The tools, in three parts

### PART ONE · DOCS AND HELP

What everything is named and how it works. Needs nothing installed.

- `help`: Explain SETTLE, KANERVA and this server. With a topic, look the word up in the glossary built from the site and its docs; "glossary" lists every name.
- `read_doc`: Read one SETTLE, KANERVA or site document by name (for example "03-syntax", "sdm", "kanerva://readme", "what"); with no name, list them.
- `list_examples`: List the tested example programs from the SETTLE docs, each with its first comment line. Filter by family or by kind (ok or error).
- `get_example`: Show one tested example: its program and the exact output (or error) the interpreter is tested to produce.
- `explain_error`: Explain a SETTLE error message: the documented cause, where it is documented, and a tested program that produces it.

### PART TWO · SETUP

Check the machine, then fetch, build and verify SETTLE and KANERVA in a folder you choose.

- `check_system`: Check this machine for what SETTLE needs (rustc, cargo, git, node) by running only version commands. Shows each command it ran.
- `setup`: Fetch, build and verify SETTLE and KANERVA in a folder. Dry run by default: returns every command and a plan id. Run it with dry_run false and confirm set to that id.
- `setup_status`: Report a setup that is still running in the background, step by step, or the last setup this server ran.

### PART THREE · USAGE

Run SETTLE programs, store and recall with a sparse distributed memory, run KANERVA.

- `run_program`: Run a SETTLE program, from a .settle file or from program text, and return what it printed, its errors and its exit code.
- `sdm_store_recall`: Write named patterns (or short texts) into a sparse distributed memory, then read one back from a noisy read-address. Shows the SETTLE program it ran.
- `kanerva_quickstart`: Run the KANERVA crate's own quickstart example: build a memory, write 300 patterns, read one back, predict capacity, refuse, a keyed note and the soft machine.

## The docs

- 49 documents as resources: the three guides and their index (`site://who-you-are/...`), the SETTLE docs (`settle://docs/...`, `settle://readme`), the KANERVA README (`kanerva://readme` and `kanerva://terms`), and the site pages (`site://...`). `read_doc` with no name lists them.
- 118 tested example programs as `settle://examples/{name}`; `list_examples` and `get_example` read them.
- The glossary of 604 names as `settle-mcp://glossary`; `help` with a topic looks one up.
- `settle-mcp://help` (the three parts and where to start), `settle-mcp://usage`, `settle-mcp://setup`, and this document as `settle-mcp://agents`.
- Prompts: `explain-settling`, `write-settle-program`, `sdm-store-recall`.

## The rules

- `setup` is a dry run until you pass `dry_run` false with the plan id it returned as `confirm`, so the person sees every command before anything runs. It never uses sudo.
- Nothing is published yet: no public package, no public URL. Use the folder or git URL the person gives you.
- Quote a number with the document or the program output it came from; the guides name their sources.
- The website is the source of truth: these files are generated from the SETTLE site, and a change belongs there.
